says: A storage failure in the runner's `ensure(time)` sets no retry alarm, because `ensure` runs in the call wrapper (Runner.ts:1719-1740), outside the drain's `Effect.onExit` retry check (Runner.ts:1894-1904). So a due whose `ensure` fails is never retried.
proof: Probe by the agent writing pull request 1189's retry law: a freshly started runner over a warm store, a one-time disk fault on a query reading `process_receipts`, then `due(500)` at clock 1000. The due failed with RecoveryStoreError and the saved alarms stayed `[null, 500]`, with no retry alarm written. Not yet a committed law.
cost: A passing storage fault at the wrong moment leaves a process's due work stranded until something else wakes it, with no error a person sees.
